neighbours.label: a comma that closes a complete clause or object phrase before a trailing addition (', where...', ', 6-4', ', or whether'), not a comma that splits a verb from its complement
fire: She spent ten years at the Berlin office, where she ran the sales team.
The champion took the final, 6-3 in the deciding set.
They reached the summit before noon, though the wind was fierce.
He sold the old farmhouse, which had been in the family for a century.
The team won the cup, especially thanks to its young goalkeeper.
We finished the report on Friday, albeit two days late.
The museum reopened its east wing, closed since the flood.
She beat the defending champion, 7-5, in the second round.
quiet: The board will decide, after a long review, the new budget.
Engineers measured, with great precision, the height of the tower.
The court must determine, in each case, the correct penalty.
The committee selects, every spring, the winners of the prize.
Inspectors examined, one by one, the damaged rail cars.
The guide explained, in simple terms, the history of the castle.
Parents and teachers define, within the law, the school rules.
The jury considered, for three days, the evidence presented.

notes: Card: every top example is ','. + pole commas follow a finished clause or object (won the match, 7-6; joined Securities, where); the - pole commas split verb and complement (determine, with high precision, ...). The output promotes 'albeit/though/especially'. Near misses are verb-splitting commas and list commas.
